title: X Feed Digest
summary: OpenAI dominated the AI side of the feed: Codex expanded onto mobile while new hooks and scoped workspace tokens pushed it further from demo toy toward real automation surface.
The smartest agent posts were about scaffolding, not raw models — tmux/jsonl wrappers, multi-layer memory, and custom harnesses kept surfacing as the real leverage points.
Developer trust is becoming a competitive variable in AI tooling. Anthropic pricing backlash stayed in the conversation, while alternative harnesses and orchestration layers picked up attention.
Macro tone turned more stagflationary: hotter PPI, a 10Y push to 4.48%, and renewed Iran oil risk all fed a scarcity/commodities bid while pressuring long-duration software and crypto.
Geopolitics stayed noisy in the background, with a reported Secret Service clash in Beijing reinforcing how tightly U.S.-China theater is now tied to the market narrative.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Codex Hooks + Scoped Tokens
items.body: OpenAI added hooks that let teams run validators, secret scans, logging, and repo-specific behaviors inside the Codex loop, alongside workspace-scoped programmatic access tokens. The practical takeaway is that Codex is getting much easier to wire into CI, internal tooling, and governed enterprise workflows.

items.title: @Dimillian: Codex Comes to ChatGPT Mobile
items.body: Codex reached the ChatGPT mobile app, with the product framed less as coding on a phone and more as remotely steering jobs already running on your laptop or devbox. That makes mobile a control surface for long-running agent work instead of a stripped-down coding environment.

items.title: @dexhorthy: Interactive Agents via tmux + JSONL
items.body: dex shared a lightweight wrapper that launches interactive agent sessions inside tmux and tails the JSONL stream for observability. It is a sharp workflow tip for anyone who wants scriptable, inspectable agent runs without waiting for full native automation parity.

items.title: @akshay_pachaar: Three-Tier Agent Memory
items.body: A useful Hermes deep dive argued for splitting agent memory into tiny always-loaded files, full-text session search, and optional external memory providers. The important idea is that durable agent behavior comes from composing fast, small memory with searchable history — not from stuffing everything into the prompt.

items.title: @poetiq_ai: Harness Design Beats Raw Model Hype
items.body: Poetiq claimed its Meta-System built a custom coding harness on Gemini 3.1 Pro that topped LiveCodeBench Pro without fine-tuning or privileged access. Whether or not the exact ranking holds, the broader signal is strong: coding benchmarks are increasingly measuring harness quality as much as base model quality.

items.title: @WatcherGuru: PPI Runs Hot Again
items.body: A widely shared macro headline flagged U.S. PPI at 6%, above expectations. In context with the rest of the feed, that strengthened the day’s stagflation read: stickier inflation, fewer easy rate-cut assumptions, and a tougher backdrop for duration-sensitive risk assets.

items.title: @CoinMarketCap: Scarcity Tape, Higher Yields
items.body: CoinMarketCap’s market rundown connected the dots cleanly: hotter CPI/PPI, a 10Y at 4.48%, stronger dollar, and renewed Iran risk helped bid wheat, silver, oil, copper, and memory names while pressuring long-duration software and leveraged crypto. It was one of the better synthesis posts in the batch because it translated macro headlines into actual winners and losers.

items.title: @BrettErickson28: Iran Still Has Oil Export Breathing Room
items.body: Using fresh satellite imagery, Brett Erickson argued Iran is still loading tankers at Kharg Island and may still have several weeks of floating and onshore storage capacity left. That matters because it weakens the immediate shut-in thesis and suggests the oil-risk premium could stay alive longer than some traders hoped.

items.title: @Polymarket: Secret Service Clash in Beijing
items.body: The splashiest geopolitical headline in the feed was a reported ‘very physical’ standoff between the U.S. Secret Service and Chinese police in Beijing. Even without a direct trade or earnings angle, it was a reminder that U.S.-China diplomacy is operating with unusually high friction under the surface.

items.title: @SahilExec: The Signup Bug Is a Race Condition
items.body: One of the better practical posts in the batch used a simple username-check example to point at a classic production failure: application-level existence checks without a database uniqueness constraint. The lesson is evergreen — correctness under concurrency belongs in the database, not just in app logic.

items.title: @josevalim: Pricing Changes Need Candor
items.body: José Valim’s take on the Anthropic backlash was less about one company and more about trust: unpopular pricing changes land better when they are explained plainly instead of being dressed up as upgrades. It is a useful reminder that developer relations can be damaged as much by framing as by the actual policy change.

items.title: @LukeGrahamWhite: Don’t Time Tech Supercycles by Numerology
items.body: Luke Graham White pushed back on neat calendar-based secular bull narratives, arguing that regime shifts depend on institutions, capital flows, and political response — not tidy year-counting. It was one of the more thoughtful macro posts in the batch because it separated structural analysis from comforting pattern-matching.
